en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Niddesa 2.1 Cittuppādakaṇḍa (The Section on the Arising of Consciousness)
2.1.1. Wholesome States of the Sense-Sphere (Kāmāvacara-kusala) 2.1.1.1.
Word-by-Word Analysis (Padabhājaniya) Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge,
having as its object a visible form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental phenomenon—
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time:
There is contact; there is feeling; there is perception; there is volition; there is mind;
there is applied thought; there is sustained thought; there is rapture; there is pleasure; there is one-pointedness of mind;

there is the faculty of faith; there is the faculty of energy; there is the faculty of mindfulness; there is the faculty of concentration; there is the faculty of wisdom; there is the faculty of mind; there is the faculty of mental joy; there is the faculty of vital energy.
There is right view, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration;
there is the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom; there is the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread;
there is non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion; there is absence of covetousness, absence of ill will, and right view.
There is moral shame, there is moral dread;
there is tranquility of body, tranquility of mind; buoyancy of body, buoyancy of mind; plasticity of body, plasticity of mind;
wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind; proficiency of body, proficiency of mind.
There is bodily pliancy, there is mental pliancy, there is bodily proficiency, there is mental proficiency, there is bodily rectitude,
there is mental rectitude, there is mindfulness, there is clear comprehension,
there is serenity, and there is insight.
There is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are wholesome.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the quality of having contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What is the feeling at that time?
Whatever mental gratification, mental pleasure, pleasant feeling born of contact with the mind-consciousness element produced by that [object], the pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact—
that is the feeling at that time.
What is perception at that time? Whatever perception,
perceiving, state of having perceived, arises at that time born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element—
this is perception at that time.
What is volition at that time?
That which at that time is volition born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element, volitional intention, the state of having willed—
this is the volition at that time.
What, at that time, is consciousness?
That which at that time is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, cognition, the aggregate of cognition, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is consciousness.
What is applied thought at that time?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind, and right intention—
this is the applied thought at that time.
What at that time is sustained thought (vicāra)?
That which at that time is movement, sustained thought, following after, close investigation, the mental state of connecting, and the state of looking closely—
this at that time is sustained thought.
What on that occasion is rapture (pīti)?
That which on that occasion is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, rejoicing in, mirth, merriment, felicity, elation, mental upliftedness—
this on that occasion is rapture.
What is pleasure at that time?
That which at that time is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mind-contact, a pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of mind-contact—
this is the pleasure at that time.
What on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind?

That which on that occasion is stability of mind, steadfastness, firmness, imperturbability, non-distraction, composure of mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration—
this on that occasion is one-pointedness of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of faith?
Whatever on that occasion is faith, being faithful, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith—
this on that occasion is the faculty of faith.
What on that occasion is the faculty of energy (vīriyindriya)?
It is the arousal of mental energy on that occasion, the striving, the exertion, the endeavor, the effort, the enterprise,
the perseverance, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the unfaltering exertion, the non-abandonment of zeal, the non-laying-down of the burden, and the grasping of the burden.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy,
and right effort— this, at that time, is the faculty of energy.
What, at that time, is the faculty of mindfulness?

Whatever at that time is mindfulness, recollection, constant mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not forgetting, the state of not lapsing, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness—
this at that time is the faculty of mindfulness.
What at that time is the faculty of concentration?

Whatever at that time is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration of the mind—
this, at that time, is the faculty of concentration.
What, at that time, is the faculty of wisdom?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom;
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena,
and right view— this, at that time, is the faculty of wisdom.
What, at that time, is the faculty of mind?

At that time, whatever is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the mind-faculty.
What, at that time, is the faculty of mental joy?
Whatever at that time is mental pleasure, mental happiness, a pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact, a pleasant and happy sensation born of mental contact—
this, at that time, is the faculty of gladness (*somanassindriya*).
What, at that time, is the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*)?
That which, for those formless phenomena, is life, stability, maintenance, sustenance, movement, persistence, preservation, vitality, and the life-faculty—
this, at that time, is the life-faculty.
What, at that time, is right view?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom;
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion,
the investigation of phenomena, and right view— at that time,
this is what constitutes right view. What, at that time, is right intention?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind,
and right intention— this, at that time, is right intention.
What, at that time, is right effort?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, exertion, endeavor, striving, effort, perseverance, fortitude, steadfastness,
unfaltering persistence, non-abandonment of desire, non-abandonment of the burden, the grasping of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort— this is [the factor of enlightenment].
At that time, this is right effort.
What at that time is right mindfulness?

That which at that time is mindfulness, constant mindfulness, specific mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, and right mindfulness.
This, at that time, is right mindfulness.
What, at that time, is right concentration?

That which, at that time, is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, and state of mental composure of the mind; serenity; the faculty of concentration; the power of concentration; and right concentration.
At that time, this is right concentration.
What, at that time, is the power of faith?
Whatever at that time is faith, believing, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, and the power of faith—this is the power of faith at that time.
This, at that time, is the power of faith.
What, at that time, is the power of energy?
It is that which, at that time, is the arousal of mental energy, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort, the perseverance, the fortitude.
Stamina, fortitude, unrelaxed persistence, non-abandonment of desire, non-abandonment of the burden, the exertion of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy,
and right effort— this, at that time, is the power of energy.
What on that occasion is the power of mindfulness (satibala)?

Whatever on that occasion is mindfulness, constant mindfulness, specific mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness—
this on that occasion is the power of mindfulness.
What on that occasion is the power of concentration?

That which on that occasion is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, serenity of mind, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—
this on that occasion is the power of concentration.
What on that occasion is the power of wisdom (*paññābala*)?
It is that which on that occasion is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment,
precise discernment, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, and intelligence.
Insight is the guide, clear comprehension is the goad, wisdom is the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom,
the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena,
and right view— this, at that time, is the power of wisdom.
What on that occasion is the power of moral shame (hiribala)?
That which on that occasion is a sense of shame, a feeling of shame where there is a reason for shame, a feeling of shame regarding the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is the power of moral shame.
What on that occasion is the power of moral dread (ottappa-bala)?
That which on that occasion is moral dread, the state of being morally dreading, the act of being morally dreading with respect to evil, unwholesome states and their attainment—
this on that occasion is the power of moral dread.
What at that time is non-greed? That which at that time is non-greed,
non-covetousness, the state of being non-covetous, lack of lust, lack of lusting, the state of being without lust, absence of longing,
and the wholesome root of non-greed— this at that time is non-greed.
What on that occasion is non-hate?
That which on that occasion is non-hate, non-hating, state of non-hating, absence of ill will, absence of malice, non-hate as a root of the wholesome—
this on that occasion is non-hate.

Insight is the guide, clear comprehension is the goad, wisdom is the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom,
the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, right view, and the root of wholesomeness which is non-delusion—
at that time, this is what constitutes non-delusion.
What on that occasion is non-covetousness? That which on that occasion is lack of greed,
lack of being greedy, state of not being greedy, absence of lust, absence of being lustful, state of not being lustful, non-covetousness, the root of wholesome states that is lack of greed—
this on that occasion is non-covetousness.
What on that occasion is non-ill-will?
That which on that occasion is non-hatred, non-hating, state of non-hating, non-ill-will, non-malice, the root of wholesome states, non-hatred—
this on that occasion is non-ill-will.
What on that occasion is right view?
It is the wisdom on that occasion which is understanding, investigation, investigation-of-states, discernment, discrimination,
differentiation, erudition, proficiency, subtlety, criticism, reflection, analysis, breadth, sagacity.
Insight is the guide, clear comprehension is the goad, wisdom is the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom,
the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena,
and right view— this, at that time, is what constitutes right view.
What on that occasion is moral shame (*hirī*)?
That which on that occasion is a sense of shame, a feeling of shame where there is a reason for shame, a shrinking back from the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is moral shame.
What on that occasion is moral dread (*ottappa*)?
That which on that occasion is moral dread, the state of being morally dreading of what should be dreaded— the dread of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is moral dread.
What at that time is bodily tranquility?

That which at that time is the tranquility, the subsiding, the calming, the complete subsiding, and the state of being completely calmed of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is bodily tranquility.
What on that occasion is serenity of mind?
That which on that occasion is the serenity, the subsiding, the allaying, the complete allaying, the state of being completely allayed of the consciousness aggregate—
this on that occasion is serenity of mind.
What at that time is buoyancy of the body?

That which at that time is the buoyancy, the state of light transformation, the lack of sluggishness, and the lack of rigidity of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is buoyancy of the body.
What on that occasion is lightness of consciousness?
That which on that occasion is lightness of the consciousness-aggregate, its buoyancy, its lack of sluggishness, its lack of rigidity—
this on that occasion is lightness of consciousness.
What, at that time, is bodily plasticity? That which, at that time,
is the plasticity, softness, non-hardness, and non-rigidity of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this, at that time, is bodily plasticity.
What on that occasion is plasticity of mind?
That which on that occasion is plasticity, malleability, absence of rigidity, absence of stiffness in the aggregate of consciousness—
this on that occasion is plasticity of mind.
What on that occasion is bodily wieldiness?
That which on that occasion is the wieldiness, the state of wieldiness, the condition of wieldiness of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this on that occasion is bodily wieldiness.
What on that occasion is mental wieldiness?
That which on that occasion is wieldiness of the consciousness aggregate, its state of wieldiness, its quality of wieldiness—
this is what on that occasion is mental wieldiness.
What at that time is bodily proficiency? That which at that time is the proficiency,
the state of proficiency, the condition of proficiency of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is bodily proficiency.
What on that occasion is proficiency of consciousness?
That which on that occasion is the proficiency, the state of proficiency, the condition of proficiency of the aggregate of consciousness—
this on that occasion is proficiency of consciousness.
What, at that time, is bodily rectitude? That which, at that time, is the straightness,
rectitude, non-crookedness, non-contraction, and non-deviousness of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this, at that time, is bodily rectitude.
What on that occasion is rectitude of consciousness? That which on that occasion is the straightness,
rectitude, absence of crookedness, absence of curvature, and absence of insincerity of the aggregate of consciousness—
this on that occasion is rectitude of consciousness.
What on that occasion is mindfulness (*sati*)? That which on that occasion is mindfulness,

constant mindfulness, mindfulness with regard to [the object], mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing hold, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness— this on that occasion is mindfulness.
What on that occasion is clear comprehension (*sampajañña*)?
It is the wisdom (*paññā*), understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena (*dhammavicaya*),
discernment, close examination, close scrutiny, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, inquiry, breadth, and intelligence present on that occasion.
Insight is the guide, clear comprehension is the goad, wisdom is the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom,
the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, and right view— at that time,
this is what constitutes clear comprehension.
What on that occasion is serenity (samatha)?

That which on that occasion is stability of mind, steadfastness, firmness, imperturbability, non-distraction, mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration—
this on that occasion is serenity.
What is insight at that time?
It is the wisdom at that time which is understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment,
precise discernment, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, and intelligence.

Insight is the guide; clear comprehension is the goad; wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, and right view—at that time, this is what constitutes insight.
What on that occasion is exertion (*paggāha*)?
It is the arousal of mental energy on that occasion, the striving, the endeavor, the perseverance, the effort, the enthusiasm, the fortitude,
the steadfastness, the firmness, the state of unrelenting endeavor, the state of not relinquishing desire, the state of not relinquishing the burden, and the firm grasping of the burden.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort—
this, at that time, is exertion. What, at that time, is non-distraction?

Whatever at that time is the steadiness, stability, steadfastness, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration in the mind—
this at that time is non-distraction. Or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena there are at that time—
These states are wholesome.
The word-by-word commentary is finished.
The first recitation section.
2.1.1.2. Section on Components (Koṭṭhāsavāra):
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three nutriments, eight faculties, a five-factored jhāna, and a five-factored path.
there is [one] feeling, there are seven powers, there are three roots, there is one contact, there is one feeling,
there is one perception, there is one volition, there is one consciousness, there is one aggregate of feeling,
there is one aggregate of perception, there is one aggregate of formations, there is one aggregate of consciousness, and there is one mind-base.
There is one mind-faculty, one mind-consciousness element, one base of mental phenomena, and one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are wholesome.
What four aggregates are present on that occasion?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
What is the aggregate of feeling on that occasion?
Whatever at that time is mental ease, mental pleasure, pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mental contact, pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of mental contact—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of feeling (*vedanākkhandha*).
What, at that time, is the aggregate of perception (*saññākkhandha*)?
Whatever at that time is perception, the act of perceiving, the state of having perceived— this, at that time,
is the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha).
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy,
the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness,
right concentration, the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, and the power of moral shame.
The power of moral dread consists of non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion; non-covetousness, non-ill will, and right view; moral shame and moral dread; serenity of body and serenity of mind;
lightness of body and lightness of mind; malleability of body and malleability of mind; wieldiness of body and wieldiness of mind; proficiency of body and proficiency of mind;
rectitude of body and rectitude of mind; mindfulness and clear comprehension; tranquility and insight; exertion and non-distraction.

Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations.
What, at that time, is the aggregate of consciousness?

At that time, whatever is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of consciousness.
These, at that time, are the four aggregates.
Which two bases are present at that time?
The mind base and the mental-phenomena base.
What is the mind base at that time?
Whatever at that time is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, or the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the mind-base (*manāyatana*).
What, at that time, is the base of mental phenomena (*dhammāyatana*)?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
at that time, these constitute the sense base of mental phenomena (dhammāyatana).
At that time, there are these two sense bases.
What two elements are present at that time?
The mind-consciousness element and the mental-object element.
What is the mind-consciousness element at that time?
Whatever at that time is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, or the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the element of mind-consciousness.
What, at that time, is the element of mental phenomena (dhammadhātu)?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
at that time, these constitute the element of phenomena (dhammadhātu).
At that time, there are these two elements.
What are the three nutriments at that time?
They are the nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental volition, and the nutriment of consciousness.
What is the nutriment of contact at that time?
Whatever at that time is contact, touching, contacting, the state of having contacted—
this, at that time, is the nutriment of contact.
What, at that time, is the nutriment of mental volition?
Whatever at that time is volition, intention, and the state of having intended—
this, at that time, is the nutriment of mental volition.
What, at that time, is the nutriment of consciousness?
Whatever at that time is mind, intellect, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, or the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the nutriment of consciousness.
These, at that time, are the three nutriments.
Which eight faculties are present at that time?
The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental joy, and the faculty of life.
What is the faculty of faith at that time?
Whatever at that time is faith, the state of being faithful, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith,
and the power of faith— this, at that time,
is the faculty of faith. What, at that time, is the faculty of energy?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort, the enthusiasm,
the perseverance, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the unfaltering exertion, the non-abandonment of desire, the non-laying down of the burden,
the grasping of the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort— this is [the factor of enlightenment].
This, at that time, is the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*).
What, at that time, is the faculty of mindfulness (*satindriya*)?

That which, at that time, is mindfulness, constant mindfulness, specific mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, and right mindfulness.
This, at that time, is the faculty of mindfulness.
What, at that time, is the faculty of concentration?

That which, at that time, is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-distraction, and non-wavering of the mind; the state of mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration.
This, at that time, is the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*).
What, at that time, is the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*)?
It is that wisdom which, at that time, is understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, and close examination.
Discernment, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, investigation, vast intelligence, wisdom, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, understanding, the faculty of understanding, the power of understanding, the sword of understanding, the palace of understanding, the light of understanding,
the radiance of understanding, the lamp of understanding, the jewel of understanding, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, and right view.
This, at that time, is the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).
What, at that time, is the faculty of mind (*manindriya*)?

That which, at that time, is the heart, the mind, the mental faculty, the heart-essence, the pure mind, the mind-base, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—this, at that time, is the faculty of mind.
This, at that time, is the faculty of mind (*manindriya*).
What, at that time, is the faculty of mental joy (*somanassindriya*)?
That which, at that time, is mental well-being, mental pleasure, the pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact—that pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact.
This, at that time, is the faculty of mental joy (*somanassindriya*).
What, at that time, is the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*)?
It is the vitality, the persistence, the maintenance, the upkeep, the carrying on, the subsistence, the preservation, the life, and the life-faculty of those immaterial phenomena.
At that time, this is the life-faculty.
At that time, these are the eight faculties.
What at that time is the five-factored jhāna?
Applied thought (*vitakka*), sustained thought (*vicāra*), rapture (*pīti*), pleasure (*sukha*), and one-pointedness of mind (*cittassekaggatā*).
What, at that time, is applied thought?
That which, at that time, is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind, and right intention.
At that time, this is what constitutes applied thought (*vitakka*).
What at that time constitutes sustained thought (*vicāra*)?
That which at that time is movement, sustained movement, following movement, close following movement, the continuous threading of the mind, and the constant scanning—that is sustained thought.
At that time, this is what constitutes sustained thought (*vicāra*).
What at that time is rapture (*pīti*)?
That which at that time is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, exultation, laughter, mirth, a sense of well-being, elation, and mental satisfaction—that is rapture at that time.
This, at that time, is rapture (pīti).
What, at that time, is pleasure (sukha)?
That which, at that time, is mental well-being (sāta), mental pleasure, born of mind-contact, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mind-contact—that is pleasure.
This, at that time, is happiness.
What, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind?

It is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-distraction, non-diffusion of mind, the state of mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—at that time.
At that time, this is the one-pointedness of mind.
At that time, this is the five-factored jhāna.
What, at that time, is the five-factored path?
Right view, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.
What, at that time, is right view?
It is the wisdom at that time which is understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, and close examination.
Discernment, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, investigation, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom,
the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, and right view.
At that time, this is right view.
What at that time is right intention?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, thought, intention, application, thorough application, the directing of the mind—this is right intention.
At that time, this is right intention.
What at that time is right effort?
It is the arousal of mental energy at that time, the striving, the exertion, the endeavor, the effort, the perseverance, and the persistence.
Stamina, fortitude, unrelaxed perseverance, non-abandonment of zeal, non-abandonment of the burden, the exertion of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort—
this, at that time, is right effort.
What on that occasion is right mindfulness (sammāsati)?

That which on that occasion is mindfulness, constant mindfulness, recollection, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not floating away, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness—
this on that occasion is right mindfulness.
What on that occasion is right concentration?

That which on that occasion is stability of mind, steadfastness, firmness, imperturbability, non-distraction, mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—
this on that occasion is right concentration.
At that time, this is the five-factored path.
What are the seven powers at that time?
The power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread.
What on that occasion is the power of faith (*saddhābala*)?
Whatever on that occasion is faith, having faith, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith—
this on that occasion is the power of faith.
What on that occasion is the power of energy?
It is the arousal of mental energy on that occasion, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort, the zeal,

the perseverance, the firmness, the fortitude, the state of not relaxing one's efforts, the state of not relinquishing one's desire, the state of not laying down the burden, and the sustained application of the burden.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy,
and right effort— this, at that time, is the power of energy.
What, at that time, is the power of mindfulness?

Whatever at that time is mindfulness, recollection, constant mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing hold, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness,
the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness— this, at that time,
is the power of mindfulness. What, at that time, is the power of concentration?

Whatever at that time is the stability, steadfastness, stability, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of non-disturbed mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—
this at that time is the power of concentration.
What at that time is the power of wisdom?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena,
discernment, examination, close examination, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, scrutiny, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom; this is called the faculty of wisdom.
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, investigation of phenomena,
and right view— this, at that time, is the power of wisdom. What, at that time, is the power of moral shame?
Whatever at that time constitutes a sense of shame, being ashamed of what should be shamed for— the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states— this, at that time,
is the power of moral shame (*hiribala*). What, at that time,
is the power of moral dread (*ottappabala*)?
Whatever sense of moral dread one feels at that time, feeling moral dread regarding what should inspire moral dread— the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states— this, at that time,
is the power of moral dread (*ottappabala*). These, at that time, are the seven powers.
What are the three roots at that time?
Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion.
What is non-greed at that time?

Whatever at that time is non-greed, the state of being without greed, the state of not being greedy, absence of lust, absence of lusting, the state of not being lustful, non-covetousness, and the wholesome root of non-greed—
this, at that time, is non-greed. What, at that time, is non-hatred?
Whatever at that time is non-hatred, the state of being without hatred, the state of having no hatred, non-malice, non-ill-will, and the wholesome root of non-hatred—
this, at that time, is non-hatred.
What, at that time, is non-delusion?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding … [as above] … non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—
this at that time is non-delusion.
These at that time are the three roots.
What on that occasion is the single contact?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted—
this on that occasion is the single contact.
What is the single feeling present at that time?
That which at that time is mental ease, mental pleasure, a pleasant and happy experience born of mind-contact, a pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact—
this is the single feeling present at that time.
What is the single perception present on that occasion?
That which on that occasion is perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived—
this is the single perception present on that occasion.
What is the single volition that exists at that time?
That which at that time is volition, deliberate intention, and the state of having willed—
that is the single volition that exists at that time.
What on that occasion is the single state of consciousness?

That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the element of mind-consciousness produced by that—
this on that occasion is the single state of consciousness.
What, at that time, is the single aggregate of feeling? That which, at that time,
is mental ease, mental pleasure, a pleasant and pleasurable experience born of mental contact, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mental contact—
this, at that time, is the single aggregate of feeling.
What at that time is the single aggregate of perception?
Whatever at that time is perception, the act of perceiving, the state of having perceived—
this at that time is the single aggregate of perception.
What, at that time, is the single aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)? Contact (phassa), volition (cetanā), applied thought (vitakka),
sustained thought (vicāra), rapture (pīti), one-pointedness of mind (cittassekaggatā), the faculty of faith (saddhindriya), the faculty of energy (vīriyindriya),

the faculty of mindfulness (satindriya), the faculty of concentration (samādhindriya), the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya), the faculty of life (jīvitindriya), right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right intention (sammāsaṅkappo), right effort (sammāvāyāmo), and right mindfulness (sammāsati).
Right concentration; the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom;

the power of moral shame, the power of moral dread; non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion; absence of covetousness, absence of ill will, right view; moral shame, moral dread; tranquility of body, tranquility of mind;
buoyancy of body, buoyancy of mind; plasticity of body, plasticity of mind; wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind.
Bodily proficiency, mental proficiency, bodily rectitude, mental rectitude, mindfulness, clear comprehension, serenity, insight, exertion,
and non-distraction; or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception,
and the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, constitutes the single aggregate of formations.
What, at that time, is the single aggregate of consciousness?

That which, at that time, is the mind, the intellect, the mental faculty, the heart, the clarity, the mind, the sphere of mind, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the single aggregate of consciousness.
What, at that time, is the single sense-sphere of mind (manāyatana)?

That which, at that time, is the heart, the mind, the mental faculty, the intellect, the pure mind, the mind, the sense-sphere of mind, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this, at that time, is the single sense-sphere of mind.
What on that occasion is the single mind-faculty (*manindriya*)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, mind-base, mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this on that occasion is the single mind-faculty.
What at that time is the single element of mind-consciousness?

That which at that time is the mind, the intellect, the mental faculty, the heart, the lucid mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness—
this at that time is the single element of mind-consciousness.
What, at that time, is the single base of mental phenomena (dhammāyatana)?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception,
and the aggregate of formations— this, at that time, is the single base of mental phenomena.
What is the single element of phenomena (dhammadhātu) at that time?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this is the single element of phenomena at that time.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are wholesome.
This concludes the section on categories.
2.1.1.3. The Section on Emptiness (Suññatavāra) At that time, however, there are mental phenomena (dhammas); there are aggregates (khandhas); there are bases (āyatanas); there are elements (dhātus);
there are nutriments (āhāras); there are faculties (indriyas); there is jhāna; there is the path (magga); there are powers (balas); and there are roots (hetus).
There is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is mind, there is the aggregate of feeling, there is the aggregate of perception,
there is the aggregate of formations, there is the aggregate of consciousness, there is the sense base of the mind, there is the faculty of the mind,
there is the element of mind-consciousness, there is the sense base of mental phenomena, and there is the element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are wholesome.
What states are present at that time?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
these, at that time, are the phenomena (dhammas).
Which aggregates are present at that time?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations,
and the aggregate of consciousness— these, at that time,
are the aggregates. What, at that time, are the sense bases?
The mind-base and the mental-object-base—
these, at that time, are the bases.
What, at that time, are the elements?
The mind-consciousness element and the mental-object element—
these are the elements at that time.
What are the nutriments at that time?
Contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—
these are the nutriments at that time.
What are the faculties at that time?

The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental pleasure, and the faculty of life—
these are the faculties at that time.
What is the jhāna at that time?
Applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind—
this, at that time, constitutes jhāna.
What, at that time, is the path?
Right view, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration—
this, at that time, constitutes the path.
What, at that time, are the powers?
The power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of moral shame,
and the power of moral dread— these are the powers at that time.
What are the roots at that time?
Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion—these, at that time, are the causes.
What, at that time, is contact? …pe…
At that time, this is contact.
What at that time is feeling? ... [as before] ...
At that time, this is feeling.
What on that occasion is perception? …pe… This on that occasion is perception.
What on that occasion is volition? …pe…
At that time, this is the volition.
What at that time is the consciousness? ... [as before] ...
At that time, this is the consciousness.
What at that time is the aggregate of feeling? …pe… This at that time is the aggregate of feeling.
What at that time is the aggregate of perception? …pe…
This, at that time, is the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha).
What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)? ...
[as before] ... This, at that time, is the aggregate of formations.
What at that time is the aggregate of consciousness?
… [as before] … this at that time is the aggregate of consciousness.
What at that time is the sense base of mind? … [as before] …
At that time, this is the mind-base (manāyatana).
What at that time is the mind-faculty (manindriya)? ...
[as above] ... At that time, this is the mind-faculty.
What at that time is the mind-consciousness element? ... [as above] ...
this at that time is the mind-consciousness element.
What at that time is the sense-base of mental phenomena?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
these at that time constitute the sense-base of mental phenomena (dhammāyatana).
What at that time constitutes the element of mental phenomena (dhammadhātu)?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations— at that time,
these constitute the element of phenomena (dhammadhātu).
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
These states are wholesome.
The section on emptiness.
The first consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and with volitional effort, having as its object a visible form … or a mental phenomenon,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on].
These states are wholesome.
This is the second consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge,
having as its object a visible form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental phenomenon—
or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, and so forth.
There is perception; there is volition; there is consciousness; there is applied thought; there is sustained thought; there is rapture; there is pleasure;
there is one-pointedness of mind; there is the faculty of faith; there is the faculty of energy;
there is the faculty of mindfulness; there is the faculty of concentration; there is the faculty of mind; there is the faculty of mental joy; there is the faculty of vital energy.
There is right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration;
there is the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread;
there is non-greed, non-hatred, lack of covetousness, lack of ill will, moral shame, and moral dread.
There is tranquility of body, tranquility of mind; buoyancy of body, buoyancy of mind;
malleability of body, malleability of mind; wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind;
proficiency of body, proficiency of mind; rectitude of body, rectitude of mind; there is mindfulness and serenity.
There is energy, there is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome …pe….
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, seven faculties, five-factored jhāna, the fourfold path,
six powers, two roots, one contact … [and so on] … one mental-object base.
There is one dharma-element;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial dharmas exist at that time—
these dharmas are wholesome … [and so on].
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness,
the faculty of concentration, the faculty of life, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, and the power of faith.

The power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread; non-greed, non-hatred, non-covetousness, non-ill will, moral shame, and moral dread;

tranquility of body, tranquility of mind, lightness of body, lightness of mind, malleability of body, malleability of mind, wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind, proficiency of body, proficiency of mind, and rectitude of body.
Rectitude of mind, mindfulness, serenity, exertion, and non-distraction; or whatever other conditioned,
immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—
this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These states are wholesome.
This is the third consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?

At whatever time a wholesome consciousness belonging to the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort, having either a visible form as its object, or ... pe ...
a mental phenomenon as its object, or whatever else it may be directed toward—at that time there is contact ... pe ... there is non-distraction ...
pe ... these states are wholesome.
The fourth consciousness.
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge—
Whether it be a visible-form object, a sound object, a smell object, a taste object, a tangible-object, or a mental-object,
or whatever else is taken as the basis— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and one-pointedness of mind.
There is the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness,
the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of life; there is right view,
right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, and the power of faith.

There is the power of faith, there is the power of energy, there is the power of mindfulness, there is the power of concentration, there is the power of wisdom, there is the power of moral shame, there is the power of moral dread;
there is non-greed, there is non-hatred, there is non-delusion; there is non-covetousness, there is non-ill will, there is right view;
there is moral shame, there is moral dread; there is tranquility of body, there is tranquility of mind.
There is lightness of body, lightness of mind; there is malleability of body, malleability of mind;
there is wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind; there is proficiency of body, proficiency of mind;
there is rectitude of body, rectitude of mind; there is mindfulness, clear comprehension, serenity, insight, and exertion.
There is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the state of being contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What on that occasion is feeling?

That which on that occasion is born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness-element, mental, neither-pleasant-nor-unpleasant, born of mind-contact, a feeling born of mind-contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—
this on that occasion is feeling …pe….
What on that occasion is equanimity (upekkhā)?

That which on that occasion is mental neither-pleasant-nor-unpleasant feeling, born of mental contact, a feeling born of mental contact that is neither-painful-nor-pleasant—this on that occasion is equanimity. …pe…
What on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity (*upekkhindriya*)?

That which on that occasion is mental, neither pleasant nor unpleasant, born of mind-contact, a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, a feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant—this on that occasion is the faculty of equanimity. …pe…
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ...
[as before] ... At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, eight faculties, a fourfold jhāna, a fivefold path,
seven powers, three roots, one contact …pe… one base of mental phenomena,
and one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome … [as before] … What,
at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy,
the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness,
right concentration, the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, and the power of moral shame.
The power of moral dread; non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion; non-covetousness, non-ill will, and right view; moral shame and moral dread; tranquility of body and tranquility of mind;
lightness of body and lightness of mind; malleability of body and malleability of mind; wieldiness of body and wieldiness of mind; proficiency of body and proficiency of mind;
rectitude of body and rectitude of mind; mindfulness and clear comprehension; serenity and insight; exertion and non-distraction.

Or whatever other dependent-originated mental states (arūpa-dhamma) exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha). ...
These states are wholesome.
The fifth consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, with volitional effort, having visible form as its object … [and so on] … [up to] … mental phenomena as its object.
Whether having mental phenomena as its object or whatever else it may be directed toward, at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … these states are wholesome.
This is the sixth consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time a wholesome consciousness belonging to the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge,
and having as its object a visible form, a sound, a smell, a taste, or a tangible object—
Whether it be mental objects as the object, or whatever else he has taken as his basis, at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind,
there is the faculty of faith, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of mindfulness, there is the faculty of concentration.
There is the faculty of mind, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of life; there is right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration;
there is the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread; there is non-greed and non-hatred.
There is non-covetousness, there is non-ill will, there is moral shame, there is moral dread; there is tranquility of body, tranquility of mind;
buoyancy of body, buoyancy of mind; plasticity of body, plasticity of mind; wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind;
proficiency of body, proficiency of mind; rectitude of body, [rectitude of mind].
There is rectitude of mind, there is mindfulness, there is serenity, there is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial states exist at that time—these states are wholesome... [and so on].
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, seven faculties, a fourfold jhāna, a fourfold path,
six powers, two roots, one contact …pe… and one mental-object base.
There is one dharma-element;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial dharmas exist at that time—these dharmas are wholesome ... [and so on] ... .
What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
It is contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy,
the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of life, right intention, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, and the power of faith.

The power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of moral shame, and the power of moral dread; non-greed, non-hatred, non-covetousness, non-ill will, moral shame, moral dread;

tranquility of body, tranquility of mind, lightness of body, lightness of mind, malleability of body, malleability of mind, wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind, proficiency of body, proficiency of mind, rectitude of body.
Rectitude of mind, mindfulness, serenity, exertion, and non-distraction; or whatever other conditioned,
immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time,
constitutes the aggregate of mental formations …pe….
These states are wholesome.
This is the seventh consciousness.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort,

having as its object a visible form …pe… or a mental phenomenon, or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are wholesome.
The eighth consciousness.
Eight great wholesome consciousnesses of the sense sphere.
